textbookText: The bench alkali is diluted to the required extent such that the diluted alkali and acid neutralize more or less in equal volumes. Then second titration is done to standardize this diluted alkali solution. By knowing the strength of the diluted alkali, the strength of the bench alkali can be calculated. The unknown strength is determined using the normality equation, Where, VI = Volume of alkali (say)
Sl = Strength of alkali V2 = Volume of acid S2 = Strength of acid
Volumetric Analysis The calculated strength in terms of normality can be converted into other terms as following relations:

Normality Molarity (Where, n = Acidity of the alkali) n Gm/ litre = Normality x Equivalent weight = Molarity x Molecular weight Percentage by volume — ¯ 10 x Gm/litre The normality factor of the primary standard solution supplied (i.e. oxalic acid solution) is calculated by the relation, Weight of solute taken Normality factor (f) = Weight of solute to be taken Molecular weight of oxalic acid (H2C204.2H20)
Equivalent weight of oxalic acid = = 63 Now, To prepare 1000 ml of N-oxalic acid solution, 63 gm of solute is needed.
To prepare 100 ml of fö- oxalic acid solution, 0.63 gm of solute is needed.
At the equivalence point, following reaction completely takes place.
H2C204 + 2NaOH Na2C204 + 2H20
PROCESS
Finding the rough strength of bench NaOH Clean all the apparatus. Wash them with distilled water.
Rinse the burette with bench NaOH. Clamp the burette to the stand and fill it with bench NaOH to the zero mark.
Rinse the pipette with the standard oxalic acid solution supplied.
Pipette out 10 ml of the acid in a conical flask. Add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein and shake gently.
Titrate the acid against the bench alkali.

Volumetric Analysis Dilution of bench alkali and titration of diluted alkali against standard acid Take exact 6 ml of bench NaOH from the burette or measuring cylinder into a 100 ml volumetric flask.
Add water little at a time shaking after each addition. Add water till the lower meniscus coincides the etched mark of the volumetric flask.
Remove the bench alkali from the burette. Wash the burette with water. Rinse the burette with the diluted alkali.
Clamp the burette to the stand. Fill the burette with the diluted alkali upto the zero mark.
Pipette out IO ml of the standard acid in a conical flask. Add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator. Shake gently.
Titrate the diluted alkali solution against the standard acid supplied.
At the end point, permanent slightly pink colour is observed.
Repeat the titraüon till at least two concurrent readings are obtained.
